summary: An excerpt from a science-fiction novel (Book 15, part 3) in which a character named Ray lies at the lip of a vertical shaft above overheated reactor tanks, delaying the descent he dreads. The narration shifts into an essay-like digression on scavengers as nature's recyclers, arguing that nature and starships are both closed environmental systems. It then describes why an engineer chose machines over biological organisms and scavenging animals for starship waste recycling, since biology could overproduce, turn hostile, and animals like hyenas and rats posed hazards to the crew.
one_line: Excerpt from a science-fiction novel where Ray stalls at a reactor shaft and digresses on scavengers and starship waste recycling.
key_facts: Ray has lain at the top of a vertical shaft for several minutes contemplating his assault on it, a delaying tactic.
The shaft's molten heat streams up from the core in waves described as thick and suffocating as a winter stack of grandma's old feather comforters.
Ray imagines he can see the lava glow of the cooling tanks four hundred meters directly below his position.
The narration says the lava-glow hallucination is unpleasant and completely fabricated, and Ray knows it.
The text states that nature is a closed environmental system.
Scavengers such as hyenas, rats and barnacles are described as recycling the detritus of other creatures.
The text states that starships are also closed environmental systems.
Laboratory biogenerate mosses, molds and single-celled organisms were once used to recycle starship waste and made travelers sick and tired.
Biological organisms had a distressing tendency to overproduce themselves and to evolve into flesh or structure devouring slimes.
An engineering geek realized that packing a starship with rats and hyenas would pose its own discomforting circumstances.
Hyenas tend to eat indiscriminately if allowed to run loose, posing a danger to the edible-looking human crew.
Live rats were described as having promiscuous reputations that would create serious population control problems.
